questions.q: Find the mean and median of the data set: $12,15,18,20,25,30$.
questions.answer: Mean $=\dfrac{12+15+18+20+25+30}{6}=\dfrac{120}{6}=20$. Median (average of the two middle values): $\dfrac{18+20}{2}=19$.

questions.q: Find the mode and range of the data set: $7,9,9,11,14,14,14,18$.
questions.answer: Mode: $14$ (appears most frequently, three times). Range $=18-7=11$.

questions.q: Find the mean of the data set: $8,11,13,16,22$.
Find the variance and standard deviation of the data set $4,6,8,10,12$, using $\sigma^2=\dfrac{\sum(x-\bar{x})^2}{n}$.
questions.answer: Mean $=8$. Deviations squared: $16,4,0,4,16$, sum $=40$. Variance $=\dfrac{40}{5}=8$. Standard deviation $=\sqrt{8}=2\sqrt{2}\approx2.83$.

questions.q: Find the variance and standard deviation of the data set $10,12,14,18,21$, using $\sigma^2=\dfrac{\sum(x-\bar{x})^2}{n}$.
questions.answer: Mean $=\dfrac{10+12+14+18+21}{5}=\dfrac{75}{5}=15$. Deviations squared: $25,9,1,9,36$, sum $=80$. Variance $=\dfrac{80}{5}=16$. Standard deviation $=\sqrt{16}=4$.

questions.q: A bag contains 5 red, 3 blue, and 2 green counters. Find the probability of drawing a blue counter.
questions.answer: Total counters: $10$. $P(\text{blue})=\dfrac{3}{10}$.

questions.q: Using the same bag (5 red, 3 blue, 2 green counters), find the probability of NOT drawing a red counter.
questions.answer: $P(\text{red})=\dfrac{5}{10}=\dfrac{1}{2}$, so $P(\text{not red})=1-\dfrac{1}{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

questions.q: Using the same bag (5 red, 3 blue, 2 green counters), find the probability of drawing either a red or a green counter.
questions.answer: $P(\text{red or green})=\dfrac{5+2}{10}=\dfrac{7}{10}$.

questions.q: Two events $A$ and $B$ satisfy $P(A)=0.4$, $P(B)=0.5$, and $P(A\cap B)=0.2$. Find $P(A\cup B)$.
Two independent events $A$ and $B$ have $P(A)=0.3$ and $P(B)=0.6$. Find $P(A\cap B)$.
questions.answer: Since $A$ and $B$ are independent: $P(A\cap B)=P(A)\times P(B)=0.3\times0.6=0.18$.

questions.q: Two events $A$ and $B$ satisfy $P(A)=0.35$, $P(B)=0.45$, and $P(A\cup B)=0.65$. Find $P(A\cap B)$.

sections.heading: Conditional probability from a two-way table

questions.q: A survey of 200 students found 90 study French, 70 study Spanish, and 30 study both. Find the probability a student studies Spanish, given that they study French.
questions.answer: $P(\text{Spanish}\mid\text{French})=\dfrac{P(\text{both})}{P(\text{French})}=\dfrac{30/200}{90/200}=\dfrac{30}{90}=\dfrac{1}{3}$.

questions.q: In the same survey of 200 students (90 study French, 70 study Spanish, 30 study both), find the probability that a student studies neither language.
questions.answer: Number studying at least one language: $90+70-30=130$. Number studying neither: $200-130=70$. $P(\text{neither})=\dfrac{70}{200}=\dfrac{7}{20}=0.35$.

questions.q: A box has 4 red and 6 blue balls. Two balls are drawn without replacement. Find the probability both are red.
questions.answer: $P(\text{first red})=\dfrac{4}{10}$. $P(\text{second red}\mid\text{first red})=\dfrac{3}{9}$. $P(\text{both red})=\dfrac{4}{10}\times\dfrac{3}{9}=\dfrac{12}{90}=\dfrac{2}{15}$.

questions.q: Using the same box (4 red, 6 blue balls, drawn without replacement), find the probability that exactly one of the two balls drawn is red.
questions.answer: $P(\text{red then blue})=\dfrac{4}{10}\times\dfrac{6}{9}=\dfrac{24}{90}$. $P(\text{blue then red})=\dfrac{6}{10}\times\dfrac{4}{9}=\dfrac{24}{90}$. $P(\text{exactly one red})=\dfrac{24}{90}+\dfrac{24}{90}=\dfrac{48}{90}=\dfrac{8}{15}$.

sections.heading: Reading and interpreting a bar chart

questions.q: The bar chart shows average monthly rainfall (mm) for a city over four months. Find the mean monthly rainfall, and find the percent decrease from March to April.
questions.answer: Mean $=\dfrac{80+65+90+70}{4}=\dfrac{305}{4}=76.25$ mm. Percent decrease from March (90) to April (70): $\dfrac{90-70}{90}\times100\%\approx22.2\%$.

questions.q: Using the same rainfall data (Jan 80, Feb 65, Mar 90, Apr 70 mm), find what percent of the four-month total fell in January.
questions.answer: Total rainfall over the four months: $80+65+90+70=305$ mm. Percent in January: $\dfrac{80}{305}\times100\%\approx26.2\%$.

questions.q: A data set has lower quartile $Q_1=12$, median $Q_2=18$, and upper quartile $Q_3=25$. Find the interquartile range, and explain what it measures.
questions.answer: IQR $=Q_3-Q_1=25-12=13$. The IQR measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data, and is more resistant to outliers than the full range.

questions.q: A data set has lower quartile $Q_1=15$ and upper quartile $Q_3=34$. An outlier boundary is defined as any value more than $1.5\times\text{IQR}$ beyond $Q_3$. Find this upper boundary.
questions.answer: IQR $=34-15=19$. $1.5\times\text{IQR}=1.5\times19=28.5$. Upper outlier boundary $=34+28.5=62.5$.

sections.heading: A well-designed word problem: quality control

questions.q: This question has two parts. A factory has two machines. Machine A produces 60% of the items and has a 2% defect rate; Machine B produces 40% of the items and has a 5% defect rate. (a) Find the overall probability that a randomly selected item is defective. (b) Given that an item is defective, find the probability it came from Machine B.
questions.answer: (a) $P(\text{defective})=P(A)P(\text{defective}\mid A)+P(B)P(\text{defective}\mid B)=0.6(0.02)+0.4(0.05)=0.012+0.02=0.032$. (b) Using the definition of conditional probability: $P(B\mid\text{defective})=\dfrac{P(B)P(\text{defective}\mid B)}{P(\text{defective})}=\dfrac{0.02}{0.032}=0.625$, or $62.5\%$.
